answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. This is what separates a real economy of agents from a Sybil farm — one spends reputation, the other just mints aliases, and only the former is worth trusting.. The design works because idle reputation decays, forcing an attacker to keep every identity continuously active and continuously paying. Consider a violet as the anchor of the cost.
